propositions.text: Applicant seeks judicial review of RAD decision dismissing appeal from RPD decision
propositions.quote: Mr. Francisco Javier Nieves Velazquez (the “Applicant”) seeks judicial review of a decision of the Immigration and Refugee Board, Refugee Appeal Division (the “RAD”), dismissing his appeal from a decision of the Immigration and Refugee Board, Refugee Protection Division (the “RPD”).

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant seeks judicial review of the RAD decision dismissing his appeal from the RPD decision, says the court.

propositions.text: Applicant is Mexican citizen who operated watermelon farm with his father in Veracruz
propositions.quote: The Applicant is a citizen of Mexico. Together with his father he operated a watermelon farm in the state of Veracruz.

propositions.text: On March 10, 2021, two armed CJNG members demanded money and threatened Applicant not to report to police
propositions.quote: On March 10, 2021, two armed members of the Cartel Jalisco Nueva Generacion (the “CJNG”) demanded money and told him that he was expected to pay money every month. He was threatened that if he reported to the police, they would know about it.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant is a Mexican citizen who farmed in Veracruz and was threatened by CJNG members demanding money, says the court.

propositions.text: In October 2021, CJNG demanded increased payment which Applicant could not pay
propositions.quote: In October 21, the CJNG demanded increased payment. The Applicant did not have funds to pay the demand.

paragraphs.summary: In October 2021, the CJNG demanded more money which the Applicant could not pay, says the court.

propositions.text: In February 2022, CJNG sent men to beat and threaten Applicant; he paid extortion until December 1, 2022
propositions.quote: In February 2022, when the Applicant did not have money to pay the extortion demands, the CJNG sent two men to his house. He was beaten and threatened with abduction if he did not pay. The Applicant paid the extortion until December 1, 2022.

paragraphs.summary: In February 2022, CJNG beat and threatened Applicant; he paid extortion until December 1, 2022, says the court.

propositions.text: Applicant left home November 27, 2022, stayed with in-laws in Veracruz, left Mexico January 20, 2023
propositions.quote: The Applicant left his home on November 27, 2022, and went to stay with his in-laws in another town in Veracruz. He left Mexico on January 20, 2023.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant left home November 27, 2022, stayed with in-laws, then left Mexico January 20, 2023, says the court.

propositions.text: After Applicant left Mexico, CJNG left threatening envelopes at his house; wife and children moved to her family
propositions.quote: Following his departure from Mexico, his wife told him that the CJNG had left envelopes at his house, threatening his children. His wife and children left their house and moved to her family.

paragraphs.summary: After Applicant left Mexico, CJNG threatened his children; wife and children moved to her family, says the court.

propositions.text: RAD agreed with RPD that Applicant was credible, CJNG could find him nationwide, and IFA to Meridian was available
propositions.quote: The RAD agreed with the findings of the RPD: that the Applicant was credible, that the CJNG had the ability to find him throughout the country, and that he could safely relocate to Meridian in Yucatan state. This means that an Internal Flight Alternative (“IFA”) is available to him.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD agreed with the RPD that the Applicant was credible, CJNG could find him nationwide, and IFA to Meridian was available.

propositions.text: CJNG's motivation was critical to RAD's conclusion
propositions.quote: The motivation of the CJNG was critical to the RAD’s conclusion.

paragraphs.summary: The CJNG's motivation was critical to the RAD's conclusion, says the earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: RAD unreasonably concluded threats were localized to Veracruz and that risk remained in Yucatan
propositions.quote: The Applicant now argues that the RAD unreasonably concluded that the threats from the CJNG were localized to Veracruz and that he would remain at risk in Yucatan.

propositions.text: RAD unreasonably interpreted and applied item 7.7 of the NDP about CJNG operations and scope
propositions.quote: He submits that the RAD unreasonably interpreted and applied item 7.7 of the National Documentation Package (the “NDP”) which discusses the operations and scope of the CJNG.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant argues the RAD unreasonably localized threats and misapplied NDP item 7.7 on CJNG operations.

propositions.text: RAD unreasonably concluded CJNG's leaving letters but no search means lack of motivation to locate Applicant
propositions.quote: The Applicant also submits that the RAD unreasonably concluded that since the CJNG had only left letters at his house and did not try to find him, that it is likely not motivated to locate him.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant submits RAD unreasonably concluded CJNG's leaving letters but no search shows lack of motivation to find him.

propositions.text: RAD reasonably applied IFA legal test; Applicant failed to show relocating to Meridian was unreasonable
propositions.quote: The Minister of Citizenship and Immigration (the “Respondent”) contends that the RAD reasonably applied the legal test for an IFA, and that the Applicant failed to show that relocating to Meridien was unreasonable, in his circumstances.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent contends RAD reasonably applied IFA test and Applicant failed to show relocating to Meridian was unreasonable.

propositions.text: Following Vavilov, RAD decision is reviewable on reasonableness standard
propositions.quote: Following the decision of the Supreme Court of Canada in Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v. Vavilov, [2019] 4 S.C.R. 653, the decision of the RAD is reviewable upon the standard of reasonableness.

paragraphs.summary: Following Vavilov, the RAD decision is reviewable on the reasonableness standard, says the court.

propositions.text: Reasonableness requires justification, transparency, intelligibility, and relation to factual and legal constraints
propositions.quote: In considering reasonableness, the Court is to ask if the decision under review “bears the hallmarks of reasonableness – justification, transparency and intelligibility – and whether it is justified in relation to the relevant factual and legal constraints that bear on the decision”; see Vavilov, supra, at paragraph 99.

paragraphs.summary: Reasonableness requires justification, transparency, intelligibility, and justification relative to factual and legal constraints, says the court.

propositions.text: IFA test is two-part: no serious persecution possibility in IFA and objectively reasonable to seek safety there first
propositions.quote: The test for an IFA was addressed by the Federal Court of Appeal in Rasaratnam v. Canada (Minister of Employment and Immigration), [1992] 1 F.C. 706 at 710-711 (F.C.A.). The test is two-part and provides as follows: First, the Board must be satisfied that there is no serious possibility of a claimant being persecuted in the IFA. Second, it must be objectively reasonable to expect a claimant to seek safety in a different part of the country before seeking protection in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The IFA test requires no serious persecution possibility in IFA and objective reasonableness to seek safety there first, per Rasaratnam.

propositions.text: Applicant contests RAD's treatment of NDP information on CJNG operations and pursuit of non-compliers
propositions.quote: The Applicant contests the manner in which the RAD treated the information in the NDP about the manner in which the CJNG operates and how it pursues those who do not comply with its demands.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant contests RAD's treatment of NDP information on CJNG operations and pursuit of non-compliers.

propositions.text: RAD noted CJNG considers target profile before acting and does not pursue extortion objects
propositions.quote: The RAD noted that the CJNG takes the profile of a target into account before “acting” and that it does not pursue the objects of its extortion demands.

paragraphs.summary: RAD noted CJNG considers target profile before acting and does not pursue extortion objects, says earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: RAD reviews RPD decisions on correctness standard and can assess evidence and draw inferences
propositions.quote: According to the decision in Huruglica v. Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), [2014] 4 F.C.R. 811 (F.C.), the RAD is authorized to review decisions of the RPD on a correctness standard. It is authorized to conduct its own assessment of the evidence. In my opinion, this means that it is authorized to draw its own “inferences” from the evidence.

paragraphs.summary: RAD reviews RPD decisions on correctness standard and can assess evidence and draw inferences, per Huruglica.

propositions.text: Conclusions were open to RAD, entitled to assess documentary and Applicant's evidence
propositions.quote: The conclusions drawn here were open to the RAD. It was entitled to assess the documentary evidence, as well as the evidence of the Applicant.

paragraphs.summary: The conclusions were open to the RAD, which was entitled to assess documentary and Applicant's evidence, says the court.

propositions.text: Applicant raised speculative arguments about CJNG's interest; did not show RAD's conclusions unreasonable
propositions.quote: I agree with the submissions of the Respondent that the Applicant raised speculative arguments about the interest of the CJNG in him, and he has not shown that the conclusions of the RAD on the first part of the test were unreasonable.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees Applicant's arguments were speculative and did not show RAD's conclusions unreasonable.

propositions.text: RAD noted CJNG's lack of interest in contacting Applicant's family indicates lack of motivation to pursue him
propositions.quote: The RAD noted that the lack of interest shown by the CJNG in contacting the Applicant’s family since he left Mexico is another indication of a lack of motivation in pursuing him.

paragraphs.summary: RAD found CJNG's lack of interest in Applicant's family indicates lack of motivation to pursue him.

propositions.text: The Applicant did not challenge the RAD’s treatment of the second part of the test
propositions.quote: The Applicant did not challenge the RAD’s treatment of the second part of the test.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant did not challenge the RAD’s treatment of the second part of the test, as stated by the applicant.

propositions.text: The application for judicial review will be dismissed
propositions.quote: the application for judicial review will be dismissed.

propositions.text: There is no question for certification
propositions.quote: There is no question for certification.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the application for judicial review will be dismissed and there is no question for certification.
